```{r setup, include=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# Load all libraries 
library(igraph)
library(fluxweb)
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
source(here::here("R_code",
                  "functions.R"))
library(brms)
library(bayestestR)
library(DescTools)
library(ggeffects)

# Load fluxes
fluxes <- 
  load_matrices(folder = here::here("data",
                                    "fluxes"),
                ending = ".txt")
  
# Load fwdata
fw_database <- 
  readr::read_rds(here::here("data",
                             "scalewebs",
                             "fw_database.rds"))

# Load site matrices
site_matrices <- 
  load_matrices(folder = here::here("data",
                                    "matrices"),
                ending = "_PM.txt") %>% 
  make_binary_matrices(matrix_list = .,
                       cutoff = 0.02)

# Biomass data
biomass_clean <- 
  readr::read_csv(here::here("data",
                             "biomass_clean.csv"))

# CPI
# Now combine these values in CP3
## For order-level do averages of values in the group
cp3_search <- 
  tibble::tibble(taxon = c("Trichoptera", "Ostracoda", "Odonata", "Toxorhynchites", 
                           "Curculionidae", "Dytiscidae", "Elateridae", "Elmidae",
                           "Hydrophilidae", "Lampyridae", "Planorbidae", "Scirtidae",
                           "Tabanidae", "Coleoptera", "Diptera"),
                 cp3_val = c(115.5, 450, 333, 60.5, 
                             60, 676.5, 730, 450,
                             270, 200, 144, 333,
                             150, 
                             (60 + 676.5 + 730 + 450 + 270 + 200 + 333) / 7,
                             (60.5 + 150) / 2))


# Get CPI
traits_CPI <- 
  fw_database$traits %>% 
  dplyr::select(bwg_name, dplyr::contains(c("ord",
                                            "subord",
                                            "family",
                                            "genus",
                                            "CP", ## CPI
                                            "FD", ## food
                                            "FG", ## feeding mode
                                            "functional_group"
  ))) %>% 
  ## Make a mock CPI column
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(CPI_crisp = ifelse(is.na(CP1)|is.na(CP2)|is.na(CP3),
                                   NA, mean(c(rep(10, CP1), rep(40, CP2), 
                                              rep(match_CP3(ord = ord, subord = subord, 
                                                            family = family, genus = genus,
                                                            cp3_search = cp3_search), 
                                                  CP3)))))

# Load stoichimetry data
# stoichiometry <- 
#   readr::read_csv(here::here("data",
#                              "stoichiometry.csv"))
## Make mock data until I get it
stoichiometry <- 
  fw_database$traits %>% 
  dplyr::select(bwg_name) %>% 
  ## Fake C, N, P content
  dplyr::mutate(N = runif(n = nrow(.), min = 0, max = 0.25),
                P = runif(n = nrow(.), min = 0, max = 0.1),
                C =  1 - P - N) 

# Convert matrices to list
fluxes_long <- 
  fluxes %>% 
  purrr::map(~ make_mat_long(matrix = .,
                             unit = "flux")) %>% 
  ## Rename flux column to raw
  purrr::map(~ dplyr::rename(.,
                             flux_raw = flux)) %>% 
  ## Convert flux data to proportion for each web
  purrr::map(~ dplyr::mutate(.,
                             flux_prop = flux_raw/sum(flux_raw))) %>% 
  ## Add name of web as column
  purrr::imap(~dplyr::mutate(.x,
                             web = .y)) %>% 
  ## Just remove those rows where consumers are resources
  purrr::map(~ dplyr::filter(.,
                             consumer %notin% c("algae", "FPOM", "CPOM",
                                                "bromeliad.tissue", "microorganisms"))) %>% 
  ## Flatten list
  purrr::list_rbind() %>% 
  ## Split web column in site and bromeliad
  tidyr::separate_wider_delim(cols = web,
                              delim = "_",
                              names = c("site", "bromeliad_id"))
# Combine for each consumer
fluxes_long_percons <- 
  fluxes_long %>% 
  ## Pool per consumer
  dplyr::select(-resource) %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(site, bromeliad_id, consumer) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(),
                                 ~sum(.))) %>% 
  ## Add data relative to consuemr
  ### traits_CPI from script 01
  dplyr::left_join(traits_CPI %>% 
                     dplyr::select(dplyr::everything()) %>% 
                     dplyr::rename_with(~paste0("cons_",.x )) %>% 
                     dplyr::rename(consumer = cons_bwg_name),
                   by = "consumer") %>% 
  ### stoichiometry from script 01
  dplyr::left_join(stoichiometry %>% 
                     dplyr::select(dplyr::everything()) %>% 
                     dplyr::rename_with(~paste0(., "_cons")) %>% 
                     dplyr::rename(consumer = bwg_name_cons),
                   by = "consumer") %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup()

# Get Gini coefficient and total energy flux for each bromeliad, 
# based on all the fluxes (i.e. not pooled per consumer, excluding zooplankton)
fluxes_long_perbrom <- 
  fluxes_long_percons %>% 
  ## Remove zooplankton
  dplyr::filter(!stringr::str_detect(string = consumer,
                                    pattern = "plankton")) %>% 
  dplyr::select(site, bromeliad_id, flux_raw, C_cons, N_cons, P_cons) %>%
  ## Group by site and bromeliad id
  dplyr::group_by(site, bromeliad_id) %>%
  ## Summarise
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(flux_raw,
                                 ~ DescTools::Gini(.),
                                 .names = "gini"),
                   dplyr::across(flux_raw,
                                 ~ sum(.),
                                 .names = "totalflow_Jy")) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  ## Add flow just to predators
  dplyr::left_join(fluxes_long_percons %>% 
                     ## Keep just predators
                     dplyr::filter(cons_functional_group %in% c("piercer", "engulfer")) %>%
                     dplyr::select(site, bromeliad_id, flux_raw) %>%
                     ## Group by site and bromeliad id
                     dplyr::group_by(site, bromeliad_id) %>%
                     ## Summarise
                     dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(flux_raw,
                                                    ~ sum(.),
                                                    .names = "predflow_Jy")),
                   by = c("site", "bromeliad_id"))


# Mock data, just CABO 
fluxes_long_percons_CABO <- 
  fluxes_long_percons %>% 
  dplyr::filter(site == "CABO")
fluxes_long_perbrom_CABO <- 
  fluxes_long_perbrom %>% 
  dplyr::filter(site == "CABO") %>% 
  ## I am getting frustrated at this so I will just do it inefficiently
  dplyr::left_join(
    fluxes_long_percons %>% 
    ## REMOVE FLUXES EQUAL TO 0
    dplyr::filter(flux_raw > 0) %>% 
    dplyr::filter(site == "CABO") %>% 
    ## Remove zooplankton
    dplyr::filter(!stringr::str_detect(string = consumer,
                                       pattern = "plankton")) %>% 
    ## Keep only detritivore functional groups
    dplyr::filter(cons_functional_group %in% c("gatherer", "scraper", "filter.feeder", "shredder")) %>% 
    dplyr::select(site, bromeliad_id, C_cons, N_cons, P_cons) %>% 
    dplyr::distinct() %>% 
    dplyr::nest_by(site, bromeliad_id) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(detr_dist = average_dist(data)),
    by = c("site", "bromeliad_id"))



```

## Data structure
The flux data is in long format, with each row being the energy flux going to a given consumer. This flux is both presented as a raw value and as the proportion of this flux in the total amount of flux in the bromeliad of interest. Then there are a bunch of columns with traits from the consumers (all from the fwdatabase). 
<br>
The crisp CPI column was calculated as the weighted mean of the fuzzy values from Régis and Olivier, with the CP3 values (unbounded interval) is from a literature search I did.
<br>
The stoichiometry values here were generated at random for each row of the data, with no intent on realism. I just generated them so that you can see the analyses I have in mind
```{r data pres 1}
dplyr::glimpse(fluxes_long_percons)
```
<br>
<br>
There is a second data frame that I will do analysis on, one in which each row represents metric summarised at the bromeliad level. Here I will just show for CABO because the distances take a while to compute. We now have the Gini index (bounded between 0 (perfect equality) and 1 (perfect inequality), measuring the inequality in energy fluxes going to consumers, the total amount of energy flowing within the bromeliad, and the average euclidean distance between detritivore stoichiometries (using the triangle formula in a 3D CNP space), which represents how dissimilar these detritivores are in their stoichiometries. The Gini index reflects evenness of energy use by consumer community and energetic overdominance. High inequality is associated with low biodiversity and stability of the system (Potapov 2019)
```{r data pres 2}
dplyr::glimpse(fluxes_long_perbrom_CABO)
```



## A few plots to start

Here are three plots of energy flux within the bromeliads, based on different values of the Gini index. The idea is that here the Gini index give us a hint on the number of channels in the web, with more channels leading to more equality (i.e. more strong, few weak fluxes), while bromeliads with little or no channel structre will be highly imbalanced.

```{r bromeliad plots, warning = FALSE, echo=FALSE}
# Plot most unequal bromeliad
plot_food_web(bromtoplot = "12706",
              sitetoplot = "CARDO",
              fluxes_long_format = fluxes_long,
              clean_biomass_data = biomass_clean,
              binary_matrices = site_matrices)

# Plot least unequal bromeliad
plot_food_web(bromtoplot = "8001",
              sitetoplot = "GAMAS",
              fluxes_long_format = fluxes_long,
              clean_biomass_data = biomass_clean,
              binary_matrices = site_matrices)

# Plot something in the middle
plot_food_web(bromtoplot = "12006",
              sitetoplot = "MAC",
              fluxes_long_format = fluxes_long,
              clean_biomass_data = biomass_clean,
              binary_matrices = site_matrices)
```


## Hypothesis 1 - Because of a faster growth and turnover rate, consumers with a low CPI and high P content will attract more energy flux than organisms with a slower growth.
Relation between P and CPI
We first need to prove our assumption that there is a link between CPI and P content, i.e. a test of the Growth Rate Hypothesis. 
<br>
```{r hyp1.1, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## Histograms
hist(log(fluxes_long_percons_CABO$cons_CPI_crisp))
hist(log(fluxes_long_percons_CABO$P_cons))
## Model with P explaining CPI 
cpi_model_P <- 
  brms::brm(log(cons_CPI_crisp) ~
              log(P_cons) + (1|bromeliad_id/site),
            iter = 5000,
            family = gaussian(),      
            control = list(adapt_delta = 0.9,
                           max_treedepth = 10),
            data = fluxes_long_percons_CABO)
## Look at the effect
bayestestR::describe_posterior(cpi_model_P)
## Plot
basic_line(model = cpi_model_P, 
           dats = fluxes_long_percons %>%
              dplyr::filter(site == "CABO"), 
           x_var = "P_cons", 
           y_var = "cons_CPI_crisp",
           scale = "log")
```

<br>
Then, we can go on and see if a higher CPI means lower energy flow
NB we are doing this in relative terms because we wouldn't want bromeliads with higher biomasses (thus more energy to flow) to artificially drive the pattern. 
```{r hyp 1.2, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## Histogram
hist(fluxes_long_percons_CABO$flux_prop)
## Model
cpi_model_fluxprop <- 
  brms::brm(flux_prop ~
              log(cons_CPI_crisp) + (1|bromeliad_id/site),
            iter = 5000,
            family = lognormal(),      
            control = list(adapt_delta = 0.92,
                           max_treedepth = 10),
            data = fluxes_long_percons_CABO %>%
              dplyr::filter(site == "CABO"))
       
## Look at the effect
bayestestR::describe_posterior(cpi_model_fluxprop)
## Plot of relative energy flow entering the consumer node vs. CPI score
basic_line(model = cpi_model_fluxprop, 
           dats = fluxes_long_percons %>%
             dplyr::filter(site == "CABO"), 
           x_var = "cons_CPI_crisp", 
           y_var= "flux_prop")
```
<br>

In these two plots, we can first see that P content and CPI are positively associated, implying that the growth rate hypothesis may not apply in our system, and that more P is associated with longer growth rates. A potential confounder would be body size, as P content tends to be lower with body size, but our results tend to go the other way. We can then see that more energy goes through organisms with slower growth rates, but that this relationship is not significant. 
<br>
These results indicate that P tends to be higher in slower-growing organisms, and that growth rate is not associated with the amount of energy accumulated by a consumer.

## Hypothesis 2 - Because organisms make feeding decisions based on their stoichiometry and that of their prey, more stoichiometric dissimilarity of consumers in a food web generates more energy channels.

```{r hyp 2, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## Histograms
hist(log(fluxes_long_perbrom_CABO$gini))
hist(log(fluxes_long_perbrom_CABO$detr_dist))
## Model with P explaining CPI 
gini_model_detrdist <- 
  brms::brm(log(gini) ~
              log(detr_dist) #+ (1|/site)
            ,
            iter = 5000,
            family = gaussian(),      
            control = list(adapt_delta = 0.9,
                           max_treedepth = 10),
            data = fluxes_long_perbrom_CABO)
## Look at the effect
bayestestR::describe_posterior(gini_model_detrdist)
## Plot
basic_line(model = gini_model_detrdist, 
           dats = fluxes_long_perbrom_CABO, 
           x_var = "detr_dist", 
           y_var = "gini",
           scale = "log")
```
<br>
Here we have no association between the channel structure and the stoichiometric dissimilarity of detritivores. This suggests that stoichiometry may not underly channel structures, potentially because phenotypic traits (e.g. different kinds of predator defense or different usage of the environment) could allow organisms with similar stoichiometries to coexist.

# Hypothesis 3 - Stoichiometric dissimilarity and productivity of food webs have a unimodal relationship, because a low dissimilarity (i.e. few channels) and a high dissimilarity (i.e. many, little connected channels) will not allow an efficient transfer of energy towards higher trophic levels.

```{r hyp 3.1, echo=FALSE, warning=F}
## Histograms
hist(log(fluxes_long_perbrom_CABO$totalflow_Jy))
hist(log(fluxes_long_perbrom_CABO$detr_dist))
## Model with P explaining CPI 
totalflow_model_detrdist <- 
  brms::brm(log(totalflow_Jy) ~
              poly(log(detr_dist), degree = 2) #+ (1|/site)
            ,
            iter = 5000,
            family = gaussian(),      
            control = list(adapt_delta = 0.9,
                           max_treedepth = 10),
            data = fluxes_long_perbrom_CABO)
## Look at the effect
bayestestR::describe_posterior(totalflow_model_detrdist)
## Plot
basic_line(model = totalflow_model_detrdist, 
           dats = fluxes_long_perbrom_CABO, 
           x_var = "detr_dist", 
           y_var = "totalflow_Jy",
           scale = "log")
```
<br>
Here can see that the total energy flow in a bromeliad follows a unimodal relationship with the stoichiometric dissimilarity of detritivores. This suggest that more channels, hence a more even parsing of resource use can sustain a more diverse community.

```{r hyp 3.2, echo=FALSE, warning=F}
## Histograms
hist(log(fluxes_long_perbrom_CABO$predflow_Jy))
hist(log(fluxes_long_perbrom_CABO$detr_dist))
## Model with P explaining CPI 
predflow_model_detrdist <- 
  brms::brm(log(totalflow_Jy) ~
              poly(log(detr_dist), degree = 2) #+ (1|/site)
            ,
            iter = 5000,
            family = gaussian(),      
            control = list(adapt_delta = 0.9,
                           max_treedepth = 10),
            data = fluxes_long_perbrom_CABO)
## Look at the effect
bayestestR::describe_posterior(predflow_model_detrdist)
## Plot
basic_line(model = predflow_model_detrdist, 
           dats = fluxes_long_perbrom_CABO, 
           x_var = "detr_dist", 
           y_var = "predflow_Jy",
           scale = "log")
```
<br>
Here, however, our relationship is not significant, so dissimilarity does not allow more predators to survive in a food web.
